subtopics.title: The CPJ — Job, Documents and Columns

questions.question: The Cash Payments Journal records:
options: All payments made from the business bank account, in date order, for one month

questions.question: The CPJ's name column records:
options: What the money was spent on

questions.question: Under the perpetual system, buying stock for cash is entered in:
options: The Trading Stock column — the asset loads directly at cost

subtopics.title: The Standard Payments — and the Drawings Trap

questions.question: The new R6 000 display fridge is recorded as:
options: An expense, because money left the bank
Sundries, detail Equipment — an asset kept for use, not an expense

questions.question: The owner transfers R2 000 to himself for personal use. The correct entry is:
options: Sundries, detail Drawings — the owner withdrawing equity, never an expense

questions.question: The sorting test for every payment is:
options: Was the payment made by EFT or cash?
Did the BUSINESS receive value — a possession, a consumed service — or did the owner?
Is the amount larger than R1 000?

questions.question: Burying drawings among expenses causes the books to:
options: Understate the business's true profit and misjudge its performance

subtopics.title: Totals, the Cross-Cast, and What Posts Where

questions.question: The CPJ cross-cast requires:
options: Trading Stock + Wages + Sundries totals to equal the Bank column total
Sundries to be the largest column

questions.question: At month end, the Bank column total of the CPJ is posted as:
options: A credit to Bank — payments reduce the asset

questions.question: Which pairing of internal controls belongs with the CPJ?
options: Payments only against approved documents, and monthly bank reconciliation against the journals
Two people counting the till at closing

subtopics.title: The Petty Cash Journal and the Imprest System

questions.question: Under the imprest system with a R500 float, at any moment:
options: Cash in the tin plus vouchers must equal exactly R500
The tin must hold R500 in cash

questions.question: Vouchers total R360 at month end. The restoration payment is:
options: R360 — the restoration always equals the voucher total, returning the float to R500

questions.question: The tin holds R95 cash and R340 in vouchers against a R500 float. This means:
options: The float was set too high
R65 is unaccounted for — the tin announces the shortfall immediately

questions.question: In the money-out diary, WHO comes before WHAT because:
options: Payments are chased payee-first when questions arise later

questions.question: Which payments earned their own lanes in Thabo's money-out diary?
options: Stock and wages — the constant traffic

questions.question: The money-out handshake states that:
options: The tin must equal the float
The lanes plus named visitors must add to exactly the Bank column total

questions.question: 'What did the SHOP get?' — for the R2 000 Thabo transferred to himself, the answer is:
options: Nothing — so the payment is drawings, the owner dipping into his own stake
A machine for years of use

questions.question: If the R2 000 hid among expenses, a bank reading the books would:
options: See the same picture either way
Judge a good shop as weaker than it truly performed

questions.question: The fridge is not a 'cost of the month' because:
options: Costs are what the month consumed; the fridge is a possession the shop keeps for years

subtopics.title: The Tin That Always Tells the Truth

questions.question: An afternoon count shows R245 cash and R255 in slips against a R500 float. The tin is:
options: Perfectly in balance — cash plus slips equals the float
Impossible to judge until month end

questions.question: The month's slips read: stamps R60, taxi R85, tea R120, cleaning R95. The refill from the bank is:
options: R360 — the refill IS the voucher total

questions.question: Why does ONE named person own the tin?
options: So every question about the tin has an address — accountability with division of duties
Because only managers may touch cash
